section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study (N=263) examining how self-compassion moderates the relationships between body comparison and body appreciation, as well as between appearance contingent self-worth and body appreciation. The study reveals that self-compassion protects women's body appreciation against these appearance-related threats, with the inverse relationships disappearing at relatively high levels of self-compassion (4.27-4.29 on a 1-5 scale). The authors acknowledge limitations including the cross-sectional correlational design, reliance on self-report data, and potential cultural differences in how self-compassion is experienced.
